factsUsed: Sequoia Capital Professor of Computer Science
computer vision, spatial intelligence and learning systems
Her work includes ImageNet, visual recognition, robotics and AI applications in healthcare.
Alfred and Rebecca Lin Professor
graph machine learning and large networks
His research connects network analysis and machine learning with social systems and computational biomedicine.
Thomas M. Siebel Professor of Machine Learning
language models and reproducible machine learning
His research investigates foundation models, model evaluation, robustness and interpretation.
Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
robot learning and reinforcement learning
Her research studies how robots learn perception and manipulation skills, including methods that adapt to new tasks.
Assistant Professor of Computer Science
visual understanding, robotics and computational cognition
His work combines computer vision and machine learning to study intelligent interaction with the physical world.
Assistant Professor of Computer Science
language technology and computational social science
Her work studies the social dimensions of language and how language systems can support people’s interactions.
Professor of Computer Science
AI assistants and computer systems
Her OVAL laboratory develops tools for finding and organizing knowledge. Her earlier work includes compilers and parallel computing.
Professor of Computer Science
human-computer interaction and social computing
He studies how to design interactive systems and social technologies, and is a senior fellow at Stanford HAI.
Associate Professor of Biomedical Data Science
reliable machine learning for health and biology
His work examines rigorous, accountable machine learning, with applications to biomedical science and healthcare.
Associate Professor of Computer Science
robot perception and manipulation
Her research investigates how robots combine sensing and learning to grasp and manipulate objects.
Paul Pigott Professor of Engineering
geometry, visual computing and robotics
His work includes algorithms for representing, analyzing and reconstructing shapes and understanding collections of images and trajectories.
Cryptography Professor
cryptography and computer security
He studies cryptographic systems, web and mobile security, and methods for analyzing the security of protocols.
Fletcher Jones Professor of Computer Science, Emeritus
algorithms and mathematical analysis
He is the author of The Art of Computer Programming and created the TeX typesetting system.
President Emeritus; Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
computer architecture and engineering education
He joined Stanford’s faculty in 1977 and later served as engineering dean, provost and university president.
Dean of Engineering; Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering
data management and engineering education
Her research covers nontraditional forms of data management. Her academic leadership includes the Computer Science Department and School of Engineering.
Professor of Chemistry; Director of Sarafan ChEM-H
chemical biology and bioorthogonal chemistry
Her research develops chemical tools for studying living systems and new approaches to treating disease. She received the 2022 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
D. H. Chen Professor of Bioengineering and Psychiatry
neural circuits and tools for neuroscience
His laboratory developed optogenetics and methods for studying intact biological tissues, including CLARITY.
Associate Professor of Bioengineering
biological physics and accessible scientific tools
His work studies computation in living matter and develops inexpensive science instruments, including Foldscope.
LCY: K. K. Lee Professor of Chemical Engineering
materials and wearable electronics
She leads research in materials for electronics and founded Stanford’s Wearable Electronics Initiative.
Professor of Molecular and Cellular Physiology
cell-surface receptors and molecular signaling
His laboratory studies the structure and activity of adrenergic receptors and how they help cells respond to signals.
Professor of Biology and Neurology
stress and neuroscience
His Stanford research profile identifies neuron death, stress and gene therapy as areas of interest.
Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professor of Psychology
motivation and people’s beliefs about themselves
Her research investigates self-conceptions, self-regulation and how these relate to achievement and interpersonal behavior.
Professor of Psychology and Organizational Behavior
social psychology, race and inequality
Her research examines racial associations and their consequences, including within the criminal justice system.
Professor of Management Science and Engineering, Emeritus
leadership, organizations and workplace behavior
He studies organizational change and innovation and is a co-founder of Stanford’s d.school.
Professor of Economics
auction design and market allocation
His work includes mechanisms for allocating radio spectrum and designing auctions.
Craig and Susan McCaw Professor of Economics
economics
His official Stanford profile lists his economics professorship and senior fellowship at the Stanford Institute for Economic Policy Research.
Director of the Hoover Institution; Professor of Political Economy
political economy and public policy
Her Stanford appointments connect the Hoover Institution, political science and business education.
Luke W. Cole Professor of Environmental Law
environmental law
She directs the Stanford Environmental Law Clinic and has an appointment in Environmental Social Sciences.
Stanford President; Bing Presidential Professor
economics and university education
He became Stanford’s president in August 2024 after serving as dean of the Graduate School of Business.
Provost, Emerita; Professor of Materials Science and Physics
physics and engineering education
Her Stanford leadership has included directing SLAC, serving as engineering dean, and serving as provost from 2017 to 2023.
Professor of Art and Art History
American art and cultural history
His scholarship examines art, historical experience and the relationship between visual culture and the humanities.
Phil and Penny Knight Professor of Creative Writing
fiction and creative writing
He teaches and writes fiction. His books include The Orphan Master’s Son and Fortune Smiles.
Professor of Geophysics and Electrical Engineering
ice sheets and radar systems
His research uses geophysical radar to investigate ice sheets, sea-level change and the interiors of icy worlds.
UPS Foundation Professor of Civil and Environmental Engineering
buildings and human wellbeing
Her research studies how built environments influence wellbeing. Her public profile lists leave from October 2026 through June 2027; virtual appearances do not imply physical presence.
Professor Emeritus of Linguistics and Computer Science
natural language understanding and machine learning
He founded Stanford’s NLP group and helped develop deep-learning methods for language, including word representations and natural language inference.
Adjunct Professor of Computer Science
machine learning and AI education
His Stanford AIMI profile describes his work in machine learning and online education, including DeepLearning.AI and Coursera.
Reynolds Professor in Humanities; Professor of Linguistics and Computer Science
language understanding and computational linguistics
His research includes conversation, language technology and connections between linguistics and the social sciences. He coauthored Speech and Language Processing.
Professor of Computer Science
computer animation, simulation and robotics
Her research develops methods for realistic human motion, humanoid control, reinforcement learning and computational biomechanics.
Stanford Provost; legal scholar
constitutional law and international law
She became Stanford’s provost in 2023 after serving as law school dean. Her research includes speech and academic freedom.

alumniSources.factsUsed: Jensen Huang earned a Stanford electrical engineering master’s degree in 1992 and co-founded NVIDIA the following year.
Larry Page earned a Stanford master’s degree in computer science. His doctoral research with Sergey Brin helped produce PageRank and Google.
Sergey Brin earned a Stanford master’s in computer science and worked with Larry Page during doctoral study to develop the technology behind Google.
Phil Knight earned his MBA at Stanford in 1962. His support helped create the Knight Management Center and the Knight-Hennessy Scholars program.
William Hewlett and David Packard studied engineering at Stanford before founding Hewlett-Packard. Their early work included electronic measurement instruments.
David Packard and William Hewlett developed their early engineering work at Stanford. Their collaboration became Hewlett-Packard in 1939.
Stanford identifies Vinton Cerf among its alumni associated with the development of Internet protocols.
Sally Ride earned Stanford undergraduate degrees in 1973 and graduate physics degrees in 1975 and 1978. She became the first American woman in space.
Mae Jemison earned a Stanford chemical engineering degree in 1977 and later trained as a physician. She became the first woman of color in space.
Stanford’s alumni directory of notable achievements includes astronaut Ellen Ochoa.
Sandra Day O’Connor graduated from Stanford Law School in 1952 and became the first woman to serve on the United States Supreme Court.
Herbert Hoover belonged to Stanford’s pioneer class and studied geology. This historical guest represents his connection to Stanford, not a present-day visitor.
John Steinbeck studied intermittently at Stanford from 1919 to 1925 and left without completing a degree. His studies helped shape his writing and interest in science.
Tiger Woods played for Stanford for two seasons and won the NCAA individual golf championship in 1996. This record identifies attendance and team history, not a Stanford degree.
Katie Ledecky completed her Stanford psychology degree in 2020. Her Cardinal teams won consecutive NCAA championships, and she returned as the 2025 Commencement speaker.
Simone Manuel helped Stanford win NCAA swimming titles in 2017 and 2018 and received the 2018 Honda Cup. She studied communication and African and African American studies.
Issa Rae created student productions and the web series Dorm Diaries during her Stanford years. She returned to deliver a Commencement address in 2021.
Stanford’s commencement archive identifies actor Sterling K. Brown as a member of the class of 1998 and its 2018 Commencement speaker.
Stanford lists actor Sigourney Weaver among its arts and entertainment alumni.
Stanford’s notable-alumni list includes technology entrepreneur Marissa Mayer.
Andrew Luck is included among Stanford’s notable football alumni.
John Elway is included among Stanford’s notable football alumni.
Nneka Ogwumike is included among Stanford’s notable basketball alumni.
Stanford’s 2026 Commencement record identifies Sundar Pichai as an MS ’95 alumnus and the keynote speaker.

alumniScope: A selected public notable-alumni and historical-guest cast, not the private alumni directory. Attendance is distinguished from graduation. Historical people are not presented as living visitors.
studentCoverage: Original 16 LinkedIn-based characters plus all 500 Stanford rows supplied in the research file. One row merges with a sourced athlete, leaving 515 student-kind characters and one athlete with an additional student affiliation. This is not an enrollment directory.
studentAccessPolicy: Retain only public names, academic fields, source URLs and supplied or observed expected completion years. No email/contact columns, portraits, social reactions, inferred age or actual locations are imported. Direct LinkedIn access remains blocked; only publicly indexed academic excerpts were used.
studentEnrollmentPolicy: All current-enrollment status remains unverified. Source-review status distinguishes the original 16 indexed LinkedIn excerpts, 500 independently inspected supplied references, and 0 supplied references not individually rechecked. The verified field is a source-review or import date, not an enrollment guarantee.
